Alicia — thanks for the clear ask. Outline below is what I’ll bring to the weekly sync; attaching a runbook + a SOW draft for procurement to review.

Proposed weekly sync (30 min):
- 5m: Quick pipeline health (expected closes, committed MRR that maps to capacity) — Sales
- 10m: Forecast -> capacity mapping (expected concurrency, 95th pct token/sec, steady vs burst profile) — Infra
- 10m: Hedge recommendation & cost impact (reserved vs burst; slot types) — Finance/Infra
- 5m: Action items & procurement next steps

Baseline hedge recommendation (initial):
- Commit 40% of our Q1 peak forecast as Reserved (dedicated slots) to lock latency and unit cost.
- Leave 40% as burst (on-demand) to handle variability.
- Keep a 20% operational buffer (short-term burst credits + cache tuning) to avoid throttling during unexpected spikes.

Why this split:
- Reserved slots reduce per-token cost ~25–30% for steady traffic and guarantee latency SLOs.
- Burst covers short, unpredictable spikes (model training windows).
- Buffer is cheaper than over-committing and lets us tune caching/batching to further lower spend.

Requested inputs before first sync (tomorrow):
- Alicia / BrightBuild: realistic weekly peak concurrency estimate (p95) and contract timing preference.
- Sales: expected ARR that will translate to sustained traffic by month.
- Procurement: redline timeline and any billing constraints.

Attachments: capacity_runbook.xlsx (capacity tiers & slot types), BrightBuild_SOW_v2.pdf (SOW draft for procurement)

I’ll propose a standing calendar invite for Mondays at 10am PT. If that works we’ll lock it and route to your procurement.

—
Logan Wright
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Looping in infra details / a practical hedging approach. Quick bullets: 

- GPU mix: BrightBuild’s profile (short bursts + medium steady) maps best to a 50/30/20 split by SKU: 50% reserved on A100-type slots (steady inference), 30% burst on cheaper T4/RTX-style pools, 20% buffer via dynamic burst credits.
- Burst latency: when burst sits on cheaper SKUs latency bump is expected; confirm BrightBuild’s latency tolerance (SLO band).
- Autoscale policy: recommend aggressive pre-warming 3–5 min before known batch windows using scheduled triggers from BrightBuild’s CI pipeline.
- Billing note: reserving increases committed spend; finance needs a simple amortization line to present to BrightBuild’s FinOps. I can produce a delta-cost sheet showing committed vs on-demand costs over 6 months.

Action items for Monday:
- Karthik: produce SKU-level cost delta sheet (reserved vs burst) — due EOD today.
- Laura: confirm pool provisioning lead time for A100 family and potential borrowing windows.
- Logan: confirm cadence and invite BrightBuild.
